body:
Swept every non-test file in ops (2656 lines across ops.go, einsum.go, eigh.go, svd.go, qr.go, cholesky.go, solvespd.go, logdet.go, softcap.go, doc.go). Conclusion: no candidate worth a task, and the reason is structural rather than a judgment call.

Loop inventory: exactly three for loops in the package (ops.go:264, ops.go:275 over sizes in Split; ops.go:342 over tensors in Stack). All three iterate over op ARITY, typically 2 to 3, never over tensor elements. Zero AtF64/SetF64/Unravel, zero math.* calls, zero go func or sync usage. None of the known high-yield patterns can apply: there is no element loop to hoist out of, no worker body to slab-allocate for, no transcendental to lift. perfscan reports no candidates for ./ops/..., and the loop inventory independently confirms that is a true negative rather than a scan miss.

No benchmark exists anywhere in the tree that would show a win from an ops change; no _test.go importing ops defines one. Any candidate here would need a new benchmark, which would then be measuring backend.

Reachability: the only non-test production importer is nn/pissa.go, calling ops.SVD once per adapter build (cold). Across all five external importers the used surface is SVD, Softmax, RoPE, SiLU, RMSNorm, LayerNorm, each a one-line eager forward. The composites that DO contain ops-side logic (Var, Std, VarDDof, Split, Stack, ExpandDims, Squeeze) have no caller outside the package tests.

One real finding, deliberately not proposed: escape analysis shows 122 heap-escape sites collapsing to one uniform pattern, three fixed allocations per op call (the Context, the variadic input slice, and the attrs struct boxed into the Attrs interface). It is genuine per-call overhead and bit-identical to remove, but it is CONSTANT per call and does not scale with tensor size, so it is deep in the noise against any kernel doing real work; removing it properly means changing whether backend.Execute retains its Context and inputs slice, which is a backend API contract question; and there is no benchmark to validate against.

Rejections with reasons: Var/Std/StdDDof chain 4 to 5 dispatches with full-size intermediates, and a fused single-pass variance would be a real win as a BACKEND kernel, but it reassociates the summation and has no caller here. VarDDof materializes a Full scale tensor at ops.go:136 to multiply by a scalar, but the tensor is already reduced by then so the cost is small and it needs a new backend primitive. Stack issues N ExpandDims-Reshape dispatches before the Concat, collapsible for axis 0 only, and whether it wins depends on whether backend Reshape copies or views. Split N Slice dispatches are minimum work. ExpandDims/Squeeze allocate one small shape slice, metadata only. Cholesky/QR/SVD/Eigh/LogDet/SolveSPD are one-line forwards over O(n^3) backend work and are cold. Einsum parses its spec inside backend.

If leverage on this dispatch path is wanted later, the work is in backend and needs a benchmark built first; the natural entry points from the ops side are Softmax, RMSNorm, RoPE and MatMul, because those are what real callers reach.
